questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify AED purpose, shockable rhythms, and early defibrillation value
questions.text: What is the main purpose of an AED during cardiac arrest?

answers.text: To analyze the heart rhythm and deliver a shock when a shockable rhythm is detected
To replace chest compressions for the entire resuscitation
To give rescue breaths automatically
To confirm the person's identity before care begins

explanations.a: An AED identifies rhythms that may need defibrillation and can deliver a shock when indicated. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: AED use does not replace high-quality CPR.
explanations.c: AEDs do not ventilate the person.
explanations.d: AEDs are used for rhythm analysis and shocks, not identity verification.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify AED purpose, shockable rhythms, and early defibrillation value
questions.text: What does defibrillation do?

answers.text: It checks the carotid pulse for the rescuer
Delivers a controlled electrical shock to interrupt an abnormal rhythm
It performs chest compressions automatically in all models
It gives oxygen through the lungs

explanations.a: The rescuer checks pulse; the AED analyzes rhythm.
explanations.b: Defibrillation uses a controlled shock to interrupt certain life-threatening abnormal rhythms. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Standard AEDs do not perform compressions.
explanations.d: Ventilation gives oxygen; defibrillation delivers electrical therapy.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify AED purpose, shockable rhythms, and early defibrillation value
questions.text: During AED skills practice, which rhythms are shockable in basic AED teaching?

answers.text: A definite pulse with normal breathing
Normal sinus rhythm with normal breathing
Ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia
Agonal gasps without rhythm analysis

explanations.a: A person with a definite pulse and normal breathing does not need defibrillation.
explanations.b: A normal rhythm with normal breathing is not a shockable cardiac arrest rhythm.
explanations.c: AEDs may advise a shock for shockable rhythms such as ventricular fibrillation and pulseless ventricular tachycardia. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Gasping alone does not determine whether a shock is needed.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.1 Identify AED purpose, shockable rhythms, and early defibrillation value
questions.text: Why is early defibrillation important?

answers.text: It eliminates the need to call for emergency help
It allows rescuers to stop CPR permanently after the first shock
It works best when delayed until the person wakes up
It improves survival chances when a shockable rhythm is present

explanations.a: AED use does not replace emergency response activation.
explanations.b: CPR usually resumes immediately after a shock.
explanations.c: Defibrillation should not be delayed when cardiac arrest is suspected.
explanations.d: Early AED use improves the chance of survival for shockable cardiac arrest rhythms. This is the correct answer.

Anterolateral placement
Both pads over the stomach
One pad on each wrist

After five minutes of CPR
Whenever the rescuer finishes documenting the event

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.2 Apply AED setup, pad placement, and universal operating steps
questions.text: During AED skills practice, where should the AED be placed when it arrives?

answers.text: At the person's side near the rescuer operating it
Across the room away from the person
Under the person's shoulders
On top of the person's chest

explanations.a: The AED should be positioned where it can be operated while CPR continues as much as possible. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: A distant AED delays pad placement and operation.
explanations.c: The AED should not be placed under the person.
explanations.d: The AED unit should not be placed on the chest where pads and compressions are needed.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.3 Apply AED rhythm analysis, shock safety, and post-shock CPR actions
questions.keyword: AED analysis shock safety and CPR resumption
questions.text: What should rescuers do immediately after a shock is delivered?

answers.text: Check the pulse for one full minute
Resume CPR starting with chest compressions
Remove the AED pads
Wait silently until EMS arrives

explanations.a: Long pulse checks delay compressions.
explanations.b: After a shock, high-quality CPR resumes immediately starting with compressions. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: Pads should remain attached for continued AED prompts.
explanations.d: Waiting without CPR reduces blood flow.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.3 Apply AED rhythm analysis, shock safety, and post-shock CPR actions
questions.keyword: AED analysis shock safety and CPR resumption
questions.text: During AED skills practice, what should rescuers do if the AED says no shock is advised?

answers.text: Assume the person has fully recovered
Give food or water
Resume CPR immediately
Turn off the AED and leave

explanations.a: No shock advised does not necessarily mean recovery.
explanations.b: Food and water are unsafe and unrelated to cardiac arrest care.
explanations.c: A no-shock prompt is followed by immediate CPR resumption unless signs of life are present. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: The AED may need to reanalyze later and CPR should continue.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.3 Apply AED rhythm analysis, shock safety, and post-shock CPR actions

questions.text: When does the AED typically prompt another rhythm check?

answers.text: After every single compression
After exactly 10 minutes without CPR
Solely after EMS arrives
After about 5 cycles or 2 minutes of CPR

explanations.a: That would create excessive interruptions.
explanations.b: AED reanalysis occurs much sooner during resuscitation.
explanations.c: AED prompts continue during the event.
explanations.d: The screenshots state the AED prompts another analysis after about 5 cycles or 2 minutes of CPR. This is the correct answer.

Move the person to a seated position

explanations.b: Touching or moving the person can interfere with analysis.
explanations.c: Compressions must pause when the AED analyzes rhythm.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: moving the person delays care and can interfere with analysis.

questions.text: On site, what should be done with a medication patch where a pad should go?

answers.text: On site, stop AED use because a patch is present
On site, remove the patch and wipe the area if it will not delay shock
On site, place the AED pad directly over the patch
On site, handle medication patches with bare hands whenever possible

explanations.a: The patch should be handled so AED use can continue.
explanations.b: Pads should not be placed over medication patches; remove and wipe when it will not delay care. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: A patch can interfere with shock delivery and may cause burns.
explanations.d: Gloves or a barrier should be used.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.4 Recognize AED pad, skin, clothing, jewelry, hair, water, and medication patch considerations
questions.text: During AED skills practice, what should be done if clothing covers the chest where AED pads need to go?

answers.text: On site, place pads over clothing to save time
On site, place pads on the back of the clothing
On site, remove the clothing covering the chest
On site, avoid AED use because clothing is present

explanations.a: Clothing prevents proper pad contact.
explanations.b: Pads must contact skin, not fabric.
explanations.c: Pads must be placed directly on bare skin. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Clothing should be removed so AED use can continue.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.4 Recognize AED pad, skin, clothing, jewelry, hair, water, and medication patch considerations
questions.text: On site, what should be done with jewelry during AED pad placement?

answers.text: On site, place pads directly over metal jewelry
On site, use jewelry as a pad conductor
On site, always delay AED use to remove all jewelry
On site, leave it unless it interferes with pad placement or contacts the pads

explanations.a: Pads should not contact jewelry.
explanations.b: Jewelry is not part of AED pad placement.
explanations.c: Unnecessary removal can delay defibrillation.
explanations.d: Jewelry does not need removal unless it interferes with pads or contacts them. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: What should be done if a pregnant person has ROSC after resuscitation?

answers.text: Place the person on the left side
Remove AED pads and send the person home
Place the person face down
Sit the person upright immediately without monitoring

explanations.a: The screenshots say to place a revived pregnant person on the left side to help blood flow. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Recovery after cardiac arrest requires emergency medical care.
explanations.c: Face-down positioning is not the taught recovery position here.
explanations.d: Answer boundary: post-resuscitation care still requires monitoring and professional care.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: What pads should be used for adults and children 8 years and older?

answers.text: Infant pads whenever available
Adult AED pads
No pads if the person is older than 8
Pads placed on clothing to reduce shock strength

explanations.a: Infant or child pads may deliver too little energy for adults.
explanations.b: Adult pads are used for adults and children 8 years and older. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: AED pads are needed for rhythm analysis and shocks.
explanations.d: Pads must be on bare skin.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: Should child pads be used on an adult?

answers.text: Yes, but only over clothing
Yes, if the adult is pregnant
No, the shock dose may be too low
Yes, child pads are always safer for adults

explanations.a: Pads must contact bare skin.
explanations.b: Pregnancy does not change the need for appropriate adult pads.
explanations.c: The screenshots state not to use child pads on an adult because the shock dose may be too low. This is the correct answer.
explanations.d: Child pads may not deliver adequate energy for an adult.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: What does AED readiness include?

answers.text: Removing AEDs from public areas to prevent use
Waiting until an emergency to check batteries
Keeping used pads for later reuse
Maintaining batteries, pads, and supplies and replacing used items

explanations.a: Public access programs aim to make AEDs available.
explanations.b: Battery issues should be managed before emergencies.
explanations.c: Answer boundary: used pads and supplies should be replaced.
explanations.d: AED readiness includes battery maintenance, pad replacement, and replacing supplies such as gloves, razors, scissors, and masks. This is the correct answer.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: At a daily briefing, a rescuer is using an AED on an adult. How should pads be placed when an implanted device is visible under the skin?

answers.text: Avoid placing pads directly over the device if possible
Place pads directly on top of the device
Do not use an AED at all
Remove the implanted device before AED use

explanations.a: Pads should not be placed directly over an implanted pacemaker or defibrillator when avoidable. This is the correct answer.
explanations.b: Direct placement over the device should be avoided if possible.
explanations.c: An implanted device does not prohibit AED use.
explanations.d: Rescuers do not remove implanted devices.

questions.name: AED Operation
questions.objective: 5.5 Recognize AED use with implanted devices, pregnancy, children 8 and older, and maintenance readiness
questions.text: Should an AED be used for a pregnant person in cardiac arrest?

answers.text: Solely after delivery occurs
Yes, use the AED when indicated
Solely if no one can perform compressions
No, AED shocks always harm the fetus

explanations.a: Defibrillation should not be delayed for delivery.
explanations.b: AED shocks should be used for a pregnant person in cardiac arrest when indicated. This is the correct answer.
explanations.c: AED use and compressions are both important.
explanations.d: The screenshots state the shock will not harm the fetus.
